newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq says signs 11 oil deals, tankers about to load.
newsitem.headline: Iraq says signs 11 oil deals, tankers about to load.

text.p: Iraq has signed 11 oil deals with foreign firms and supertankers are about to load Iraqi crude at terminals on the Mediteranean and the Gulf, a senior Iraqi oil official said on Sunday.

"We have signed 11 deals so far and have no problems with U.N. overseers supervising the contracts. Three supertankers are expected to lift Iraqi crude from terminals in Turkey and the Gulf today," Saddam Hassan, chairman of the State Organisation for the Marketing of Oil (SOMO) told Reuters.

Hassan denied reports the U.N. oil overseers had rejected any contracts SOMO sent for clearance: "No contract was sent back to us. Our deals are authentic and signed by all parties concerned, including the United Nations."
He did not say if all 11 contracts were cleared by the United Nations and would not disclose the names of the 11 companies.
The United Nations said on Friday it had cleared five contracts and had none pending. It had reported some earlier contracts were rejected, but said they could be resubmitted.
Iraq on Tuesday began oil exports worth $2 billion over six months under a U.N. deal to buy humanitarian needs for its people, under sweeping trade sanctions since Iraq's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
Both the sale of crude and purchase of needs like food and medicine are under strict U.N. monitoring.
Turkish state oil company TUPRAS received permission to buy 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) of Iraqi oil on Tuesday, the first contract approved.
An additional four contracts were okayed on Thursday, including contracts believed to be from U.S.-firm Coastal Corp and France's Elf Aquitaine.
Hassan said three deals had gone into effect but gave no details.

He said two tankers were to load Iraqi crude from Mina al-Bakr terminal in the Gulf on Sunday. The government has invited foreign reporters to a ceremony at the terminal to mark the loading of the first tanker since U.N. sanctions were imposed on Iraq.
Hassan declined to identify the companies with which Iraq was dealing but said SOMO, Iraq's marketing arm, was keen to win back past clients.
"We are trying to spread the limited amounts of exports over the largest possible number of potential clients of Iraqi crude. We need to have our clients back," he said.
Oil officials say demand for Iraqi crude is higher than the limit of about 650,000 barrels per day permitted under current prices.

Iraq's official press said on Sunday Iraqi experts guided a Bahamas-flagged supertanker able to carry two million tonnes of Iraqi crude to a platform at Mina al-Bakr. The official Iraqi News Agency (INA) said a second supertanker had anchored at the terminal on Sunday.
"This refutes a BBC report that Mina al-Bakr is not completely fit for exports," trumpeted the government newspaper al-Jumhouriya in a front-page article.
